text:
marie_support: Hey team — Acme (acct: acme_ops) hit a spike in tail latency on their Dedicated EU cluster this morning. They reported multiple request IDs with large downstream token latencies. Can SRE/infra help gather a repro bundle (pod logs, node dmesg, nvidia-smi snapshot, DCGM metrics) and confirm whether this is hardware/GPU or runtime?

marie_support: Request IDs: req-6f4a2b1c, req-6f4a2b1d, req-6f4a2b20. Model served: redwood-1-large (pinned v1.3.2). Time window: 2026-03-15T08:03:10Z -> 2026-03-15T08:08:00Z.

sam_engineer: repro curl they ran (sanitized):
```bash
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://api.redwood-inference.eu/v1/generate \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1-large","input":"<redacted>","max_tokens":256,"request_id":"req-6f4a2b1c"}'
```

sam_engineer: I attached a tiny trace from the app side: the client sees server stream stall between token 42-60 for ~1.9s, then normal. Looks like KV cache miss + a long kernel stall?

dave_oncall: Thanks. Can someone run the debug bundle helper on the reserved node(s)? We need: pod logs for the serving pods, kubelet logs for the nodes, `dmesg | tail -n 200`, `journalctl -u containerd --no-pager --since "5m ago"`, `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,temperature.gpu --format=csv -l 1 -f /tmp/gpu-snap.csv` and DCGM snapshots. Also note the pod name and the node name for the timestamps.

rachel_sre: If you have node name, run: `sudo rd-debug-bundle --node NODE123 --since "2026-03-15T08:00:00Z" --until "2026-03-15T08:10:00Z" --include-gpu --include-kernel --output /tmp/acme-debug-1839504321.tar.gz`

rachel_sre: That helper captures pod logs, kubelet, containerd logs, dmesg, and calls `dcgmi dmon` for DCGM. If you can't run sudo, we can spawn a privileged job to collect.

marie_support: opsbot created a debug ticket while we coordinated: DBG-ACME-183950. Please add the bundle tar.gz file there.

opsbot: Debug bundle job queued: DBG-ACME-183950. Run ID: 8b7e9f. You can check status at https://console.redwood-inference.internal/debug/8b7e9f

ivan_gpu_telemetry: Pushed a short GPU metrics excerpt from telemetry for the node that hosted that pod (node host-eu-07):
```
timestamp,util_gpu,util_mem,mem_used_mb,temperature
2026-03-15T08:02:59Z,12,6,1024,67
2026-03-15T08:03:45Z,98,92,12340,83  # spike during incident
2026-03-15T08:03:46Z,3,2,12080,82
2026-03-15T08:04:10Z,15,9,1025,68
```

ivan_gpu_telemetry: That 98% util row is interesting — possible sudden busy kernel. I'll correlate with DCGM events and nvlink errors.

sam_engineer: I grepped the serving logs (pod redwood-serve-5f8c9) and found repeated `cudaMalloc` failures right before the stall: `CUDARuntimeError: out of memory` followed by retries. But the pod is pinned 16GB; curious. Attaching two snippets: pod logs show OOM on alloc then successful fallback to quantized path (which explains delay).

acme_ops: ETA on root cause? We rely on tail latency for customer-facing chat. Also are any of these debug artifacts PII? We need to ensure PII is redacted before sharing.

rachel_sre: Good Q on PII. The bundle tool automatically removes user-supplied request body text (we mask inputs) but we need to enable `--scrub-headers` when generating if you want auth headers removed. We can also run a grep scrub for emails/SSNs on the bundle before handing over.

dave_oncall: For next steps: 1) run the rd-debug-bundle command on host-eu-07 using the time window; 2) attach the resulting tar.gz to DBG-ACME-183950; 3) ops will triage DCGM + dmesg for GPU hangs. If anyone can't run sudo, tell me and I'll schedule a quick privileged job.

marie_support: I kicked off the privileged job (no sudo required). Job ID: job-4f6c. It will upload to the debug ticket when done.

opsbot: Privileged collector started: job-4f6c. Expected run ~3-5m. Output will be attached to DBG-ACME-183950 when finished.

ivan_gpu_telemetry: I'll start correlating the DCGM timeline now. If the bundle contains `nv-host-eu-07-dcgm.json` and `nvidia-smi.log`, ping me and I'll join the postmortem.

sam_engineer: Quick note: the service-side trace shows model fallback to quantized kernels at the exact timestamp of req-6f4a2b1c. That matches the cudaMalloc OOM logs. If confirmed, this may be a memory fragmentation issue or transient spike from co-scheduled job.

acme_ops: Thanks — please confirm we will not share raw user messages. We need sanitized artifacts or a redacted bundle.

marie_support: Confirmed. Debug bundle will be scrubbed by default; I'll add an extra manual scan before release.

dave_oncall: Once bundle uploads, I'll look at kernel backtraces if any, and check for XIDs in dmesg. If we see persistent cuda errors, we can shift the tenant to a different reservation and run a stress test to reproduce.

marie_support: Filing follow-up: I'll update ticket DBG-ACME-183950 with job-4f6c status and attach the bundle when available. Will @mention here when done. :thumbsup:
